about: TESTOPS-10 AC3: twenty real assertions from the CotW run cotw-levels-20261121T215534,
hand-labelled before the analyser was changed. The sample is every fourth assertion in the
run's distinct assertion texts, sorted, first twenty - a rule fixed before any label was
written, so the sample was not chosen to flatter the result.
The label is the interaction whose evidence settles the claim in the scenario it belongs to:
I1  the store's own state (a row, a file the builder wrote, a fingerprint)
I2  a response the tool sends (status, exit status, JSON body, an error naming the offender)
KP  the page as served (rendered markup, a page's body text, a data-* attribute)
I3  data reaching the presentation (never labelled here: with no browser it reads as KP)
I4  what a browser computes (the accessibility tree, a control's reachability)
'binding_layer' is the layer the step's own definition calls, read from Steps/*.cs, and
'uses_browser' is whether any step of the scenario drives a browser. Both are inputs the
analyser is allowed to use, recorded here so the test needs no repository.
sample_rule: sorted distinct assertion_text, every fourth, first twenty

samples.assertion: a report file is written that can be read without running the tool again
samples.scenario: The report is a plain readable file naming every fact checked
samples.why: the claim is that a file exists on disk and reads without the tool; the file is the evidence

samples.assertion: each entry carries an id, a display name and a fact count
samples.scenario: Searching characters returns id, display name and fact count
samples.why: the entries are fields of the JSON body the list endpoint returns

samples.assertion: each fact is shown with its quotation inline
samples.scenario: Proposals are grouped into one sheet per entity with quotations inline
samples.why: the step reads the served sheet page's visible text; no person acts on it

samples.assertion: each fact's data-fact-id is the same on both loads
samples.scenario: Every rendered fact is anchored by a stable data-fact-id
samples.why: the claim is an attribute of the served markup, read twice; the browser is not what decides it

samples.assertion: each shows its value, its citation and the whole verbatim paragraph
samples.scenario: A sheet page renders every fact with value, citation and whole paragraph
samples.why: the sheet page's body carries the value, citation and paragraph

samples.assertion: every interactive control exposes an accessible name
samples.scenario: Every control has an accessible name
samples.why: the name a control exposes is computed by the accessibility tree

samples.assertion: every stored fact is reported as passing
samples.scenario: A clean store is reported fact by fact as passing
samples.why: the claim is about the pass's answer over the facts in the store

samples.assertion: it is not an empty successful response
samples.scenario: An unknown character id returns 404 naming the id
samples.why: the response's status and body settle it

samples.assertion: it names the table the fact was wrongly placed in
samples.scenario: A Tier 2 row found in the facts table is reported as a failure
samples.why: the audit's report over stored rows is the evidence

samples.assertion: it reports the number of sheets
samples.scenario: Health reports the sheet count and fact count
samples.why: the health endpoint's JSON body reports the count

samples.assertion: no finding names the unapproved proposal
samples.scenario: An unapproved proposal is invisible to every detector
samples.why: the detectors read the store; their findings are its content

samples.assertion: that fact is not in the canon store
samples.scenario: Rejecting one fact within a sheet excludes only that fact
samples.why: a fact id present or absent in the canon file

samples.assertion: that fingerprint is not the claim text itself
samples.scenario: The record carries an approval fingerprint distinct from the claim
samples.why: a value recorded in the stored row

samples.assertion: the Tier 2 fact is admitted
samples.scenario: The two rules do not satisfy each other
samples.why: whether the row reached the store

samples.assertion: the canon store contains one fact per admitted proposal
samples.scenario: Approving a sheet admits each fact individually and records a batch review
samples.why: a count of rows in the canon file

samples.assertion: the clean store exits with the success status
samples.scenario: Exit status alone distinguishes pass from failure
samples.why: the exit status is the tool's answer, not a fact in the store

samples.assertion: the groups appear in publication order
samples.scenario: A character's facts are grouped by book in publication order
samples.why: the order of the groups in the JSON body the facts endpoint returns

samples.assertion: the page claims no character name contains "Qqqzzx"
samples.scenario: The empty canon, the unmatched term and the unsearched list are three answers
samples.why: a sentence in the served page's body

samples.assertion: the page's search state is "not-searched"
samples.scenario: The empty canon, the unmatched term and the unsearched list are three answers
samples.why: a value the served page reports

samples.assertion: the rejected fact is not in the canon store
samples.scenario: Rejecting one fact within a sheet excludes only that fact
samples.why: a fact id present or absent in the canon file
